Black_Knot.quote: The first symptoms appear in the fall as swellings on twigs, which enlarge the next season, gradually encircle the stem, and form black galls.
Once established, black knot is easily identified with its hard, uneven, black galls that seem to enwrap twigs and branches.

Powdery_Mildew.quote: This fungal disease initially produces a light green, circular spot on either leaf surface, and later a characteristic white, powdery coating of the fungus appears, typically on the underside of affected leaves.
The shoots may also become covered with the fungus. Diseased tissues are often deformed and stunted.
Infected fruits develop round, depressed areas which may not show any fungal growth. Older infections may cover the entire fruit.
